page: Amazon Web Services m8i.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration delivers 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core running at 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory comprises 256 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance includes no discrete GPUs and provides no local NVMe storage, directing all disk I/O through networked storage services over a 30 Gbps baseline network connection.

Benchmark evaluations position the m8i.16xlarge in the top 10 percent of servers for multi-core compute and compilation pipelines, scoring 21,499 on Geekbench multi-core and 59,463 on Clang compilation benchmarks. The underlying Intel architecture incorporates Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets, driving strong throughput on CPU-based machine learning inference, with medium-model (7B) prompt processing reaching 298.38 tokens per second. Memory subsystem tests demonstrate 196.85 GB/s uncached large-block read bandwidth alongside static web serving throughput of 107.39 GB/s.

By omitting local ephemeral disks and dedicated graphics hardware, the instance maximizes resource density for central processing and system memory. Cost efficiency is driven by high multi-threaded utilization and hardware acceleration for vector and matrix mathematics without the overhead of GPU provisioning. It is well suited for large CI/CD build farms, static web hosting clusters, in-memory caching engines like Redis, and containerized backend microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates 256 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz alongside a large 480 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but provides no local storage or GPUs, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Benchmark profiles place it in the top decile for Geekbench multi-core performance, Clang software compilation, and static web serving throughput. Hardware-level acceleration features such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX facilitate competitive LLM prompt evaluation and high-throughput data processing. The instance delivers a balanced hardware profile well suited for enterprise application servers, distributed compilation, Redis caching layers, and high-concurrency web platforms requiring substantial multi-core density.
